title: My Grandson Hadn’t Visited Me in Three Weeks. Then I Found Him Locked in the Basement.

author: Admin

blocks.text: My 12-year-old grandson, Leo, had not visited me for three weeks.
That may not sound like a long time to some people.
Since my son David died in a boating accident four years earlier, Leo had spent nearly every Saturday at my house.
I would wake up early, make cinnamon cereal—the kind he loved even though he always complained that I put too much milk in it—and wait for the sound of his footsteps on my porch.
We would sit on the porch in the afternoon, drinking warm milk while Leo told me about school, his friends, and whatever strange new thing he’d learned that week.
After David died, those Saturdays became more than a routine.
They were the closest thing I had left to my son.
So when Leo missed one Saturday, I called his mother, Karen.
“You really need to stop worrying,” she said. “You’re making this harder than it needs to be.”
That was when I knew something was wrong.
The next morning, I drove to their house.
When I turned onto their street, I immediately noticed something strange.
No signs of a twelve-year-old boy living there.
I parked across the street and walked toward the front door.
Several family photographs had disappeared from the walls.
Even the kitchen cupboards were nearly bare.
Why would Karen tell me they were fine when the house looked as if they were moving away?
It had always been kept closed because the basement was mostly storage.
But now there was a heavy padlock attached to the outside.
Why would anyone lock a basement from the outside?
While I waited, I kept talking to Leo through the door.
A few minutes later, the police arrived.
When the door opened, Leo was sitting on an old mattress in the corner.
There was a bottle of water beside him and a small plate with a few pieces of bread.
I rushed forward, but one of the officers stopped me briefly while they checked the room.
David had never mentioned a secret account to me.
“I don’t know,” Leo said. “But Mom saw me holding it.”
That evening, Leo was taken to the hospital for examination.
Thankfully, he wasn’t seriously injured.
But what happened next changed the entire story.
The flash drive contained financial documents.
And something that made my stomach turn.
There were records showing that someone had been withdrawing money from an account connected to my late son.
The withdrawals had begun shortly after David’s death.
It was being transferred to an account belonging to a man named Michael Reed.
And that’s when we discovered the truth.
He wasn’t some stranger she had met online.
He was David’s former business associate.
Apparently, before David died, he had discovered that Michael had been stealing from their company.
The police had always considered the boating accident exactly that—a tragic accident.
And investigators discovered something horrifying.
David’s boat hadn’t simply malfunctioned.
For four years, everyone had believed my son died in an accident.
But the biggest shock was still waiting for us.
Then they showed her the financial records.
She admitted she had discovered what David knew about Michael after his death.
Instead of going to the police, she became part of the scheme.
She had been receiving money to keep quiet.
But Leo had accidentally discovered the evidence.
That’s why she locked him in the basement.
She wasn’t planning to keep him there forever.
She was planning to disappear with Michael.
And she needed Leo out of the way first.
But there was one question I couldn’t stop asking.
Why hadn’t Karen simply taken Leo with her?
The answer came from something found inside the house.
The police handed it to me several days later.
My son had written it months before his death.
